dedupe_keys.name: national zoning atlas u s zoning district data

description: The National Zoning Atlas is digitising and standardising information on zoning conditions in the more than 33,000 zoning jurisdictions of the United States, through an interactive map and Zoning Snapshots, to inform changes that allow more and better housing. Its team extracts more than 200 regulatory characteristics for each zoning district, deciphers geospatial files and digitises old hand-drawn maps so districts can be compared on the same terms. It is run by Land Use Atlas, Inc., a non-profit founded by Sara Bronin; it began with Connecticut in 2021, which showed 91% of that state's land zoned for single-family housing and 2% allowing multi-family housing, and has since expanded to more states, with a Maryland atlas launch announced on the site for 6 October. More than 500 people have contributed. Coverage: states and jurisdictions completed so far, not yet the whole country. Access: free interactive map; the dataset has DOI 10.4079/zoning-atlas. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): all rights reserved (no use without written permission, per the site terms). Caveats: coverage is partial and zoning codes change after coding. Simulation uses are allowed density and use constraints for housing supply and building stock growth scenarios. Related records: the NYC Zoning Tax Lot Database.
